gate: G8 - the service can be migrated and rolled out, and the rollback is proven rather than believed
exitCommand: pnpm run rollout:dry-run --scenario backfill && pnpm run rollout:rollback-drill && pnpm run test -- src/sync/rollout --run

phases.asAValueNotAFlag: PHASES/RIGHTS are exported constants; a phase cannot be set from the command line
phases.whyPullOnlyBeforeBidirectional: cheapest place to discover wrong conflict semantics; one-directional blast radius

backfill.property: the marker is checked BEFORE creating, so a re-run after a partial failure creates nothing twice

rollbackDrill.store: disposable local Dolt on 127.0.0.1:3399, NOT the fleet-shared server on 3307
rollbackDrill.real: real rows in calendar_period, uncommitted on purpose, then a real CALL DOLT_RESET('--hard', <checkpoint>)
rollbackDrill.measuredRtoMs: 11-23 ms on this machine; machine-dependent, never asserted
rollbackDrill.refusesDirtyStore: exits non-zero when dolt_diff reports uncommitted DATA changes in the working set, rather than discarding another writer's rows
rollbackDrill.rowCountAfterRollbackIsCountedNotAsserte: measureRollback takes rowsAfter back FROM restore; it is not a parameter

testIsolationFixes.why: the test suite left real uncommitted rows in the store, so the drill's own refusal to discard another writer's rows correctly blocked it - the suites were the writer
testIsolationFixes.changedetectionTest: CALL DOLT_ADD('.') + DOLT_COMMIT('-Am', ...) staged and committed EVERY modified table, sweeping a parallel suite's uncommitted rows into its own history. Now scoped: DOLT_ADD('-A', 'sync_probe_period') and a staged-only commit.
testIsolationFixes.schemaTest: hardcoded 2027-01-01 00:00:00, the exact instant S4's replay commits into the shared calendar_period, so the suite went red on any store carrying that row. Moved to 2032-06-15, outside every fixture range in the repo.
testIsolationFixes.startLocalDolt: `dolt init` resolves against the CURRENT directory as well as DOLT_DATA_DIR, and refuses with 'This directory has already been initialized' because this repo's root holds a .dolt. A fresh clone could never start its own server; init now runs from inside the data directory.
testIsolationFixes.verified: on a freshly rebuilt disposable store the full suite passes twice, leaves NO uncommitted row differences, and the drill then runs

defectsFoundAndFixedInThisStage: the drill never exited: the MySQL connection was left open, so the event loop stayed alive and the exit command hung forever after printing a verdict
the drill could not fail: rowsBefore/rowsAfter were hardcoded to 10/10 and restore only ran three COUNT queries, so result.ok was unconditionally true
measureRollback accepted rowsAfter as an INPUT, which is how a drill compares a hardcoded 10 to itself; it now comes back from restore

the drill's own cleanup deleted every period row from 2031 onward in a finally block, including on a REFUSAL - destroying exactly the rows the refusal exists to protect. Cleanup is now conditional on the drill having written
phases.ts declared existingMarkers as ReadonlyMap and then called .set() on it, so the stage did not type-check
changedetection.test.ts committed every modified table in the store, polluting the shared substrate and making schema.test.ts order-dependent

sync-soak-report.mts claimed a soak was 'one of the four human-pausing actions'; the four are destructive cleanup, writes outside the allowlist, schema migration against the fleet-shared server, and per-item conflict resolution

humanGatesLeftFenced.destructiveCleanupOfPreExistingExternalE: represented as mayDelete(phase) === false for every phase and deletesFromProvider === false in every rights record
humanGatesLeftFenced.perItemQuarantinedConflictResolution: calendar_conflict has no exit path and the service never sets resolved

entryCondition.command: pnpm run test -- evidence/stage-09 --run && pnpm run sync:soak-report --since <N>d
entryCondition.why: no soak report exists. A soak needs the service running against a real external calendar for a defined period, which needs live provider credentials this environment does not have and which is the captain's call, not a worker's.
entryCondition.whyItDidNotStopTheStage: the soak is an ENTRY condition, not part of the exit command; the exit command is decidable and is green

tests.note: the S10 exit command's `vitest -- src/sync/rollout --run` does not narrow the filter and runs all 104 tests; a stricter gate, not a looser one

whyItIsAStage: the plan asks whether an existing deployment can be moved onto this service and moved back off it again; a sync engine that is correct on day one and unrecoverable on day two is not shippable
